newsitem.title: GERMANY: Simens head appeals for more company wage autonomy.
newsitem.headline: Simens head appeals for more company wage autonomy.

text.p: The head of German electronics giant Siemens AG appealed to wage partner to allow individual companies more leeway in determining their wage structures.

In a summary of an interview to be published in Monday's edition of German newspaper Die Welt, Heinrich von Pierer warned Germany's system of industry-wide wage contracts would be doomed to collapse unless companies had more room to manoeuvre on wage contracts.

He said that companies, if pressed would exit the industry federations which now negotiate the industry-wide wages contracts with unions. "Companies could then try to negotiate deals that meet only the legal minimum," von Pierer said.
Von Pierer said Germany's high tax and wage costs must be cut in order to make the nation more attractive for investors and urged the government to take action.
He also said that more capital should be made available to entrepeneurs to start small businesses and welcomed first steps made in this direction.
